I am an economist in the Infrastructure and Energy Sector of the Inter-American Development Bank. I received my PhD in Economics from Brown University.

My research is in development economics, with a focus on Latin America. I study how institutions and infrastructure shape economic development. My current work examines who controls and governs water, how electricity systems respond to drought, and how transportation infrastructure, trade, and land reform shape regional development over the long run.
